A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and are readable throughout, including their appendices. The retained algorithms, theorems, proofs and Figure 1 can be matched despite renumbering, relocation and substantial theoretical additions.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical algorithms, analytical constructions and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes. Figure 1 illustrates distributions used in a proof.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout. Its additional closeness-testing results and expanded appendices present mathematical arguments, not empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds a closeness tester for two sequences of distributions using three samples per source, heavy/light partitioning, cross-distribution collisions and randomized redistribution of heavy-element samples. This is a new procedure beyond v1's learning and uniformity/identity algorithms, which are retained.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation scenarios. The new closeness problem is treated theoretically, and the added LLM-data example is motivation rather than evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The added discussion of prior closeness testers provides theoretical positioning, not new evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. The new three-sample requirement and heavy/light sampling procedure specify a theoretical algorithm rather than changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests or case studies. The added analyses concern mathematical guarantees and their limitations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Revised variance and Gaussian-approximation bounds are theoretical proof changes, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical scores, result tables or observed experimental findings. The new sample-complexity guarantees and revised analytical bounds are formal results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds the closeness theorem and Appendix G proofs, revises Section 3's covariance expansion, and replaces Appendix A's Chernoff/union-bound proof with a second-moment argument. Lemma 5.6 becomes CLT Lemmas 9–10 with explicit support assumptions and stronger origin-mass conditions; Appendix F adds substantial Gaussian and discretization arguments alongside relocated lemmas.

C1.justification: Closeness testing moves from future work in v1 to a central contribution in v2's abstract, Theorem 1.7 and conclusion: three samples per distribution suffice with O(k^(2/3)/epsilon^(8/3)) total samples. The original uniformity, identity and pooled-sample impossibility claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 1.2 and Remark 5 add explanations of the missing variance cancellations and suboptimal epsilon dependence. They also explain the three-sample design, discuss possible two-sample closeness testing, and give a sufficient near-identical-distribution condition under which one-sample testing becomes feasible.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation, hardware, runtime or code/data-release information. The added thresholds and sampling constructions describe mathematical algorithms rather than implementation or experimental reproducibility details.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion and citations for closeness testing, notably Batu et al. (2013) and Chan et al. (2014), plus Horn and Johnson (2012) for matrix facts. The existing positioning against other non-identical-sampling research largely remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 adds dedicated Future Directions and Conclusion sections, edits wording and author information, modularizes proof exposition, and moves two existing technical lemmas into Appendix F.

P2.justification: The TMLR format changes the title/author arrangement, running headers, typography and equation wrapping. Figure 1 retains identical artwork but is resized and repositioned; no new figures or tables appear.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the uniformity variance expansion and makes several lower-bound arguments and limitations more explicit. However, its new closeness contribution has unresolved support: Theorem 1.7 omits Appendix G Theorem 36's epsilon > k^(-1/3) restriction, and Lemma 33, Equations (28)–(29), drops conditioning on a heavy-element set selected from the same samples without justification. These material proof issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the useful revisions.
